why: the run stamped PRODUCT_PROMISING on a DEV-only archive whose null bar was not held to the same drawdown refusal as the arm, and whose finalists were mostly evaluated on ONE window bank; both inflate the excess and neither is visible in the headline

defect_1_the_null_is_not_held_to_the_arm.what: WindowBank draws its 6 null genomes with random_genome() and no admissibility check, while every scored genome had to survive the derived drawdown refusal first. The refusal rejected 5,348 of 7,721 candidates (69.3%).
defect_1_the_null_is_not_held_to_the_arm.so: the fitness is 'an ADMISSIBLE genome minus a TYPICAL genome', not admissible minus admissible. Whatever the drawdown filter selects for beyond drawdown itself is credited to the signal.
defect_1_the_null_is_not_held_to_the_arm.direction: inflates the excess; the magnitude is unmeasured
defect_1_the_null_is_not_held_to_the_arm.fix: apply the same admissible() gate to the null draws inside WindowBank.__init__ -- one line, and it makes the bar the arm's own population
defect_1_the_null_is_not_held_to_the_arm.family: the same asymmetry RW2 and N2 found in other lanes on 2026-09-09, here in this job's own code

defect_2_the_archive_still_ranks_on_one_.what: the archive ranks a genome by the MEDIAN of its fitness across the banks it met, which was the correction to ranking by its BEST bank. But the receipt's own finalist_basis reads 'ALL lineages (only 3 met two banks)'.
defect_2_the_archive_still_ranks_on_one_.so: for almost every lineage the median is a median of ONE draw, so a genome that drew a lucky bank still outranks a genome tested twice. The multi-bank robustness the design intended did not happen.
defect_2_the_archive_still_ranks_on_one_.direction: inflates the ranking, not necessarily the level
defect_2_the_archive_still_ranks_on_one_.fix: make banks_met >= 2 an ELIGIBILITY condition for the archive rather than a preference, and re-evaluate the surviving elites on a fixed audit bank each generation so the count accumulates

what_still_stands: the archive bank is drawn from a seed the search never saw, and all 12 finalists keep a POSITIVE median excess on it -- that is a real within-DEV out-of-bank check and it is the number worth carrying: best +20.261%/yr against +28.637 on the selection banks, a shrinkage of 8.376 pp (29%).
the drawdown budget derived from the window is the correct form and it bound hard: 69.3% of candidates refused, against the 91% starvation a flat 0.35 produced and the ~0% a penalty term produces.
ancestry de-duplication works: 595 genomes collapse to 251 lineages (0.422), so a count over the archive is a count over lineages, not over relatives.
NO HOLDOUT WAS READ. 2016-2024 is untouched by this job.
corrected_reading: G3 demonstrates the protocol change and produces a DEV archive whose finalists survive a window bank they were not selected on with a 29% shrinkage. It does NOT establish a product candidate: the null bar is easier than the arm's own gate, the finalists are mostly single-bank, and no era test or holdout has been applied. Treat the +20.261%/yr as an upper bound on a DEV-only quantity.
next_step: re-run with the two one-line fixes above, then apply the roadmap 10.2 era rule (excess minus dispersion >= 0.15 in every start era) to the surviving lineages before any holdout is considered
